View each equality as an equation of functions transported across equivalences.

- For the first conjunct, rewrite the left side as
  \[
  \varepsilon_2^{-1}\circ f\circ\varepsilon_1^{-1}=f'.
  \]
  Compose with \(\varepsilon_2\) on the left and \(\varepsilon_1\) on the right, using inverse cancellation. This gives exactly
  \[
  f=\varepsilon_2\circ f'\circ\varepsilon_1,
  \]
  the right side. Function extensionality can expose the cancellations pointwise.

- For the outer `Iff`, establish both propositions independently:
  1. For every equivalence \(e\), prove
     \[
     e^{-1}\circ g=f \iff g=e\circ f
     \]
     by the same inverse-cancellation argument.
  2. Show `Equiv.ofBijective f f.bijective = f` using `Equiv.ext`, since both equivalences have the same underlying function.

Thus the main mechanism throughout is extensional equality of functions together with the left- and right-inverse identities of an equivalence.
